newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile sees stronger growth after Canada accord.
newsitem.headline: Chile sees stronger growth after Canada accord.

text.p: The Chilean government expects the free-trade treaty with Canada ratified by the Senate on Wednesday to boost annual economic growth by 0.15 of a percentage point, Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said Thursday.
"Taking into account the benefits for the different sectors, our models show that the gross domestic product will rise 0.15 percent in the long term," Aninat said at a news conference.
Chile's economy, the most robust in Latin America, is expected to grow by about six percent this year.

The pact will erase tariffs immediately on 70 percent of Chilean exports to Canada and on 90 percent of Canadian shipments to Chile. Duties on other products will fall gradually over the next 18 years.
The deal will cut prices of consumer goods, and the increase in trade should lead to greater competitivity -- both factors that will stimulate economic growth, Aninat said.
Chilean officials have said the treaty could bring a fivefold increase in bilateral trade, currently about $670 million a year, over the next decade.
Canada is already the second-largest foreign investor in Chile with billions of dollars invested, mainly in the mining industry.
Chile hopes the treaty will lay the groundwork for its long-delayed membership of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which links Canada, Mexico and the United States.

Chile was invited to join NAFTA in 1994 but talks ground to a halt after the failure by the U.S. Congress to approve fast-track powers for trade negotiators. Fast-track authority would prevent U.S. lawmakers from revising any proposed agreement before voting on whether to approve it.
